code_patch.solution:
import numpy as np


def exact_topk(queries, base, k):
    """Exact L2 top-k ids (ground truth), best first, ties by lower id."""
    d = ((queries[:, None, :] - base[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
    return np.argsort(d, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :k]


def ann_recall_at_k(exact_ids, approx_ids):
    """Mean over queries of |exact ∩ approx| / k. Entries of -1 are padding."""
    exact_ids = np.asarray(exact_ids)
    approx_ids = np.asarray(approx_ids)
    k = exact_ids.shape[1]
    hits = [len(set(e.tolist()) & (set(a.tolist()) - {-1}))
            for e, a in zip(exact_ids, approx_ids)]
    return float(np.mean(hits)) / k


class ToyIVF:
    """Inverted-file index: k-means coarse quantiser, exact rerank inside probed lists."""

    def __init__(self, base, nlist, seed=0, iters=15):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.base = base
        cent = base[rng.choice(len(base), nlist, replace=False)].copy()
        for _ in range(iters):
            assign = self._nearest(base, cent, 1)[:, 0]
            for c in range(nlist):
                members = base[assign == c]
                if len(members):
                    cent[c] = members.mean(axis=0)
        self.cent = cent
        assign = self._nearest(base, cent, 1)[:, 0]
        self.lists = [np.flatnonzero(assign == c) for c in range(nlist)]

    @staticmethod
    def _nearest(x, cent, n):
        d = ((x[:, None, :] - cent[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
        return np.argsort(d, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :n]

    def search(self, queries, k, nprobe):
        out = np.full((len(queries), k), -1, dtype=np.int64)
        probes = self._nearest(queries, self.cent, nprobe)
        for qi, q in enumerate(queries):
            cand = np.concatenate([self.lists[c] for c in probes[qi]])
            if len(cand) == 0:
                continue
            d = ((self.base[cand] - q) ** 2).sum(axis=1)
            top = cand[np.argsort(d, kind="stable")[:k]]
            out[qi, :len(top)] = top
        return out

issues.claim: appends new chunks with fresh random IDs on every run and never removes chunks of changed or deleted pages
issues.problem: Internally inconsistent with the 4%/night growth: if every page were re-inserted with random IDs each night the index would roughly double nightly (about 100% of base per run), not grow 4%. The diagnosis must fit all three symptoms.
issues.replacement: inserts new chunks under new IDs for every page it treats as changed and never removes the old chunks of changed or deleted pages

issues.claim: Each night every page is re-chunked and inserted with a new ID (random UUID or counter). Unchanged pages therefore add exact duplicates (the paragraph appears three times after three runs), edited pages add a new version while the old chunks stay (stale content), and deleted pages are never removed (answers quoting removed policies). Index growth of a few percent a night comes from edits plus any chunks whose boundaries shift when text near the start of a document changes, which can alter every following chunk.
issues.problem: Same inconsistency: 'unchanged pages add exact duplicates' on every run implies ~100% nightly growth, contradicting 'a few percent a night' stated in the next sentence and in the question.
issues.replacement: Each night the pages the job treats as changed (edited, or merely re-dated) are re-chunked and inserted under new IDs (random UUID, counter or version-stamped key) without removing the previous chunks. Every edit therefore adds a full new copy of that page while the old copy stays: a paragraph that survived three edits exists three times (duplicates), superseded wording stays retrievable (stale content), and deleted pages are never removed (answers quoting removed policies). A few percent growth per night fits this only if a small share of pages is rewritten per night; if the job re-inserted every unchanged page too, the index would roughly double each night, so check growth against the number of changed pages. Boundary shifts make it worse: an edit near the start of a document can move every following fixed-size chunk boundary, so even untouched text gets new chunk hashes and is re-inserted.

difficulty_rationale: Maps symptoms to a cause then designs idempotent update with deletion safety and rollback; multi-step design.

issues.claim: and attach metadata {doc_id, version, active:true}. 2) Upsert all new chunks (they become searchable once the index refresh completes). 3) After the upsert is confirmed, set active:false on, or delete by filter, all chunks where doc_id matches and version < new version. Queries add the filter active=true (or version = current version via a lookup table), so a mid-update query sees either only old chunks or a mix that the filter limits to a single consistent version.
issues.problem: As written, new chunks are active:true from step 2 while old ones stay active until step 3, so a query in between sees both versions (duplicate/contradictory text); the claim of a single consistent version is false.
issues.replacement: and attach metadata {doc_id, version, active:false}. 2) Upsert all new chunks; they stay invisible because queries always filter on active=true. 3) After the upsert is confirmed and refreshed, flip the new chunks to active:true, then set the old versions (same doc_id, version < new version) to active:false or delete them by filter. Activating first leaves a short window where both versions are visible; deactivating first leaves a short gap with neither, so choose per product, or avoid both with a per-document current_version pointer that queries filter on.
